newsitem.title: USA: High Plains customer cancels contract.
newsitem.headline: High Plains customer cancels contract.

text.p: High Plains Corp said Thursday that a customer which had contracted to buy ten million gallons of industrial grade ethanol over a one year period has requested the agreement be cancelled, citing force majeure.

According to the customer, government action closing the Russian borders to alcohol importing has affected the entire European Industrial Grade market and resulted in a tightening of U.S. exports, High Plains said in a statement.
High Plains is the only publicly traded company whose sole business is ethanol.

High Plains said it does have alternative markets for the product. It said it currently has customers interested in buying at least part of this product at prices up to $1.43 per gallon, which is less than the $1.70 sale price per gallon it had initially contracted for.
The company added that the price still represents a greater profit potential than the current fuel grade spot price of $1.10.

The customer that cancelled the contract has indicated its belief that the market oversupply situation is temporary and has expressed willingness to consider another purchase agreement when the export market situation improves.

"It is unfortunate that the customer has chosen to formally cancel the contract," said High Plains President Raymond Friend. "We were aware that the markets had been affected, but the customer had previously indicated a willingness to keep the contract in force, and to take the product when market conditions improved," and certain smell and taste requirements were met, he said in a statement.
